noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

name.description: Alternative name for a field used only during serialization.

hidden.description: If true then this field will not be serialized.

include.description:
Specify which fields should be sent when instances of this type are serialized. Note that this allows methods to be
included as though they were data fields, as well as pare down the actual data fields that are included in the
JSON. By default, only data fields (not constants, not methods) are sent.

This is keyed by the {@link Action.Requirement}, so different sets of fields may be serialized for different client SDKs.

```type
@ser(include={"js-client": "magnitude", "py-ipython": "magnitude"})
type Complex {
  r: !double
  i: !double

  magnitude: cached member function(): !double
}
```

In the example above, this works because the `magnitude` is marked with `cached`. It only makes sense to use this
feature on methods which are pure functions since the client then has a cached version of the function's return
value.

Serialization of an instance will return JSON like:
```json
{ "type": "Complex", "r": 3.0, "i": -4.0, "magnitude": 5.0 }
```

If you want the same behavior across different {@link Action.Requirement} then use include directly as a string
```type
@ser(include="magnitude")
type Complex {
  r: !double
  i: !double

  magnitude: cached member function(): !double
}
```

This is for use with {@link Obj} types only. Non-Obj types ({@link Value values}) should explicitly mixin
{@link Serializable} and implement custom serialization if needed.

@see Serialized
@see Include

includeCachedMethods.description:
Specify that _cached_ member methods with no parameters (except "fail" flags) should be sent as well as data
fields when instances of this type is serialized. This is a convenience to avoid having to specify all the method
names in the #include field.

This is keyed by the actionRequirement, so different sets of fields may be serialized for different client SDKs.

This is for use with {@link Obj} types only. Non-Obj types ({@link Value values}) should explicitly mixin
{@link Serializable} and implement custom serialization if needed.

@see #include

dateTimeFormat.description:
Specifies the datetime format to use when serializing datetime fields.
This guides the serdeser for serialization when the DateTime format is ambiguous,
allowing customization of how datetime values are represented in the serialized output.

The format follows the pattern syntax compatible with java.text.SimpleDateFormat.
Common examples:
- "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" for standard datetime format
- "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'" for ISO 8601 format with milliseconds
- "MM/dd/yyyy" for date-only format

If not specified, the default datetime serialization format will be used.

@see {@link DateTimeFormat}

title:
Annotation to customize C3 Type serialization. Note this should only be used in exceptional cases. E.g. when
integrating with external data source or when implementing backwards compatibility layer.
